title: Effectiveness of Neuroactive Reflex Therapy regarding the motor development and health-related quality of life of children with Infantile Cerebral Palsy
summary: Neuroactive Reflex Therapy (NART) is a therapy concept aimed at children and adolescents with early childhood brain damage, peripheral nervous system injuries, traumatic brain injuries, spastic paralysis, or severe scoliosis. The study investigates whether children treated with NART achieve improvements in motor skills as well as subjective quality of life.

interventions.name: All participants will receive the NART.

A selection of participants will undergo a control examination before the start of therapy and subsequently have a therapy-free interval of 4 weeks. After that, an initial examination will begin similar to Arm 1, and the participants will also receive the NART.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
ICP with movement disorders such as spasticity, dyskinesia, ataxia, and mixed forms
Exclusion criteria:
Epilepsy
